fix: Change `Shared::targets` to `RefCell<Rc<[Rc<Target<T>>]>>`. Rebuild the Rc in `bind` (after the push) and when `refresh` drops a dead target from the retain (both are rare, build or teardown only). Then clone the Rc here: `let targets = Rc::clone(&shared.targets.borrow());`. Every pointer move through `refresh` then does no heap allocation.

Return a borrow instead of a clone: `fn drag_of(spec: &Motion) -> Option<&Drag> { spec.drag.as_ref().map(|drag| &drag.0) }`. In `drag_update` and `drag_end` take the snapshot first: `let spec = node.spec(); let Some(drag) = drag_of(&spec) else { return };`. `spec()` is an Rc clone. This removes a deep clone of `Drag` per pointer move, including the `Vec<Offset>` inside `Release::SnapTo`.

Stop cloning the behavior list per call. Store behaviors as `RefCell<Rc<[Rc<dyn SiteBehavior>]>>` and have `behaviors()` return the `Rc<[..]>` (a refcount bump). The same change covers the calls at lines 206 and 230. Alternatively, iterate the borrowed slice in place without holding the borrow across the callback.

Store `geometry_listeners` as `RefCell<Rc<[Rc<dyn GeometryListener>]>>`, replacing the Rc on registration, which is build-time work. Then clone the Rc here: `let listeners = Rc::clone(&node.geometry_listeners.borrow());` and iterate it. This avoids a Vec allocation for every node whose laid-out geometry changes.

Avoid the Vec clone in `wants`: add `pub(crate) fn any_behavior_wants_geometry(&self) -> bool` on `MotionNode` that iterates `self.behaviors.borrow().iter().any(|b| b.wants_geometry())`, and call it here instead of `node.behaviors().iter().any(...)`. Alternatively, make `behaviors()` return an `Rc<[..]>` as described in the dragging.rs:220 finding.
